findings.contract_expects: RestaurantCard.cuisines: array of strings (openapi.yaml:7228-7231), populated from the restaurant's cuisine associations — rendered as the card subtitle line.
findings.backend_emits: cuisines is hardcoded to an empty slice [] for every card. The restaurantRow struct has no cuisines field and cardColumns SELECT never joins restaurant_cuisine for output; the table is used only for filtering (repo.go:149-152). toCard sets Cuisines: []string{} unconditionally (mappers.go:32).
findings.evidence: openapi.yaml:7228-7231 (cuisines array) vs services/hg/internal/catalog/mappers.go:32 (Cuisines: []string{}) and services/hg/internal/catalog/repo.go:30-57 (restaurantRow has no cuisines field). Consumed by RestaurantCard.tsx:83 `summariseCuisines(restaurant.cuisines)` which renders the cuisines subtitle; empty array => the cuisine line silently disappears on every card across discovery, feed, search and detail. Non-crashing (empty array is valid) but the browse surface loses all cuisine labels.

verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed real by reading contract, Go DTO/mapper/repo, and the frontend consumer.

CONTRACT (contracts/openapi.yaml:7228-7231): RestaurantCard.cuisines is `type: array, items: {type: string}`. It is NOT in `required: [id, name, halal, availability]`, and the schema deliberately omits additionalProperties (it is an allOf base). So an empty array is technically contract-valid, but the field is clearly meant to carry the restaurant's cuisine labels.

BACKEND EMITS EMPTY (services/hg/internal/catalog/mappers.go:32): toCard sets `Cuisines: []string{}` unconditionally. The DTO field exists and is serialized (dto.go:41: `Cuisines []string \`json:"cuisines"\``), but nothing ever populates it. A grep across the entire catalog package finds only these two cuisines references — no other code path fills it.

REPO CANNOT SUPPLY IT (repo.go:30-57, 61-68): restaurantRow has no cuisines field; the shared cardColumns SELECT list (repo.go:61-68) joins only halal_certificate and halal_issuing_body, never restaurant_cuisine for projection. restaurant_cuisine is referenced only inside a filtering EXISTS subquery (repo.go:149-152), so it is used to gate results but never to read cuisine names out. scanCard (repo.go:81-101) has no cuisines destination. The struct/SQL are structurally incapable of emitting cuisines. This holds for both list (listVisible) and detail (getVisible) since both use cardColumns.

FRONTEND IMPACT (packages/ui-web + ui-native src/content/RestaurantCard.tsx): the card renders the cuisine subtitle line only `when cuisines.length > 0` (web lines 68, 115-118) and drops the cuisine phrase from the accessibility label likewise (lines 283-284). An always-empty array => the cuisine subtitle silently disappears on every restaurant card across discovery, feed, search, and detail.

SEVERITY: The auditor's own rubric reserves critical/high for halal / app-crash / money. This drift touches none of those: it is non-crashing (empty array is valid JSON, no client throws), does not affect the halal badge/seal (that is a separate populated path via toHalalBadge), and has no money or auth implication. It is a real, systematic missing-data drift on a user-visible-but-cosmetic subtitle field. That is a genuine medium — real and affecting every browse surface, but not crash/halal/money. Correcting claimed severity high -> medium.

findings.backend_emits: availabilityInputDTO (services/hg/internal/restaurant/dto.go:96-99) reads `is_available` (bool) + `out_of_stock_until`. The handler decodes with decodeStrict/DisallowUnknownFields (handler.go:521), so a contract-correct client sending `availability_state` gets 422 (unknown field) and the required field is never honoured; the backend instead expects a boolean the contract does not define.
findings.evidence: openapi.yaml:9490-9505 (MenuItemAvailabilityInput: availability_state enum) vs services/hg/internal/restaurant/dto.go:96-99 + handler.go:520-523. When restaurant-web wires this endpoint it will send availability_state per the generated client and be rejected.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against contract and code. Contract MenuItemAvailabilityInput (openapi.yaml:9402-9414) has additionalProperties:false, required:[availability_state] with enum [AVAILABLE, OUT_OF_STOCK] and optional nullable out_of_stock_until; the requestBody at PUT /v1/restaurant/menu/items/{itemId}/availability (line 3091-3096) is required and refs this schema. Backend availabilityInputDTO (dto.go:96-99) instead reads is_available (bool) + out_of_stock_until — there is NO availability_state json tag. The handler (handler.go:520-521) decodes via decodeStrict, which calls DisallowUnknownFields (decode.go:15-17). The bool is genuinely load-bearing: the repo (repo_reads.go:687-705) derives the DB enum column availability_state from in.IsAvailable ('AVAILABLE' if true else 'OUT_OF_STOCK'), so this is not a benign alias. A contract-conformant client (generated api-client) sends {"availability_state":...} and gets a 422 for the unknown field; and even absent strict mode, is_available would default to false, forcing OUT_OF_STOCK. The endpoint is unusable by any contract-correct caller — restaurant-web wiring it will be rejected as claimed. This is a real wrong_field_name drift. I downgrade severity from high to medium: it is a hard, ships-broken breakage but confined to a single restaurant-menu endpoint returning 422, with no halal-safety, money-integrity, or app-crash impact (the tiers reserved for high/critical). No data corruption or invariant violation.

findings.contract_expects: Cart.restaurant is oneOf[RestaurantCard, null]; RestaurantCard requires [id, name, halal, availability]. A non-empty cart is bound to one restaurant, so a populated RestaurantCard (including the halal seal) is expected — the cart is where the halal claim for the chosen restaurant is re-asserted before checkout.
findings.backend_emits: cartToDTO (map.go:57-83) never assigns d.Restaurant; the field is typed `any` in cartDTO (dto.go:18) and left nil, so the wire always emits "restaurant": null even though loadCart (cart_store.go:94-107) loaded c.RestaurantID and c.RestaurantName from the DB. The RestaurantCard and its required halal seal are unconditionally absent from every cart response.
findings.evidence: openapi.yaml:7610-7613 (Cart.restaurant oneOf RestaurantCard/null) + openapi.yaml:7206-7212 (RestaurantCard required id,name,halal,availability) vs services/hg/internal/orders/map.go:57-83 (cartToDTO omits Restaurant) and cart_store.go:106-107 (RestaurantName loaded but dropped). CartScreen.tsx:159 `cart.restaurant ?` / :161 `cart.restaurant.name` — guarded so no crash, but the restaurant header name and the halal seal silently never render on the cart. Halal claim absent on the cart surface.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified against both sources.

CONTRACT (contracts/openapi.yaml): Cart.restaurant is oneOf[RestaurantCard, null] (~line 7610). RestaurantCard (~line 7205) has `required: [id, name, halal, availability]`, where `halal` -> HalalBadge and `availability` -> RestaurantAvailabilityInfo. So when Cart.restaurant is a populated object it MUST carry the halal seal. Note: `restaurant` is NOT in Cart.required[] (required is [id, lines, indicative_subtotal_cents, currency, is_quotable]), so emitting null is not a strict schema-validation failure — but the schema and the C-19 description intend a bound cart to carry its restaurant, and the halal claim is meant to be re-asserted here before checkout.

BACKEND: cartDTO (dto.go:17) declares `Restaurant any json:"restaurant"`. cartToDTO (map.go:57-83) never assigns d.Restaurant, so it stays nil and marshals to `"restaurant": null` on every response. GetCart handler (handlers.go:118-124) and the mutating cart handlers (lines 153,172,182) all serialize via cartToDTO, so this is the sole cart projection. Worse than the claim states: loadCart (cart_store.go:94-107) only SELECTs c.id, c.restaurant_id, r.display_name, c.delivery_address_id — it loads RestaurantID and RestaurantName but never fetches any halal certification data at all, and the Cart domain struct (cart_store.go:15-30) has no halal field. So the RestaurantCard, and specifically its required `halal` HalalBadge, is unconditionally absent from every cart response.

CLIENT: CartScreen.tsx guards with `cart.restaurant ?` so there is no crash — but the restaurant header and halal seal silently never render on the cart surface.

SEVERITY: critical. Per the rubric, halal-visibility issues are critical. The cart is a halal re-assertion surface (product's single claim is verification, invariant #8). The seal is guaranteed-absent by construction on a surface where it is contractually specified to appear. Client fails safe (no optimistic badge), which prevents an app-crash/haram-mislabel, but the required halal presentation is missing platform-wide.

findings.contract_expects: 200 response body is the full Cart; Cart.restaurant should carry the populated RestaurantCard (with halal) once a line has been added, since add-to-cart establishes the single restaurant the cart is bound to.
findings.backend_emits: AddCartLine (handlers.go:127-154) responds via the same cartToDTO which never populates restaurant; the recomputed cart returned after an add always has "restaurant": null. Same defect applies to updateCartLine, removeCartLine (all route through cartToDTO).
findings.evidence: openapi.yaml:1644-1655 (addCartLine 200 -> Cart) + openapi.yaml:7610-7613 vs services/hg/internal/orders/map.go:57-83 (cartToDTO shared by all cart handlers). The cart header restaurant + halal seal never appear immediately after the user adds an item from RestaurantScreen.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED REAL.

Contract side: The Cart schema (openapi.yaml:7599-7660) defines `restaurant` as `oneOf: [RestaurantCard, null]`. It is not in Cart.required[], and null is a legal value, so a plain schema read would not force population. BUT the canonical contract fixture cart_single_line.json is explicitly tagged `operations: ["getCart", "addCartLine"]` and populates `restaurant` with a full RestaurantCard including the required `halal` badge and `availability`. cart_empty.json (no lines) sets `restaurant: null`. Together these establish the intended contract behavior: restaurant is null only when the cart is empty, and must carry the populated RestaurantCard (with halal) once a line has been added. The claim's characterization matches the fixtures exactly.

Backend side: cartToDTO (map.go:57-83) builds cartDTO{} and never assigns d.Restaurant. The struct field is `Restaurant any \`json:"restaurant"\`` (dto.go:18), which defaults to nil and thus always serializes as `"restaurant": null`. All cart handlers route through cartToDTO — GetCart (handlers.go:118-125), AddCartLine (handlers.go:127-154), UpdateCartLine, RemoveCartLine — so every one returns restaurant:null unconditionally. The defect is real for addCartLine and its siblings as claimed.

Added nuance (not a refutation): the domain Cart struct (cart_store.go:15-30) only carries RestaurantID + RestaurantName — populated by loadCart at cart_store.go:106-107 — not the full RestaurantCard (no halal, availability, cuisines, rating, images). So the fix is broader than a one-line mapper assignment: the store's cart query must also join to fetch the halal/availability/card data. But this makes the drift worse, not weaker: the backend cannot currently emit the required RestaurantCard at all.

Severity: high (not critical). The dropped field includes the halal badge, which is the platform's single load-bearing claim, and the cart header on RestaurantScreen after add-to-cart cannot render the halal seal. That is a halal-surface defect, warranting high. It is not critical because null → renders no badge is the safe fallback the platform mandates (invariant 8: a missing halal field renders no badge, never an optimistic one), so no false halal claim is made and no money path is affected. The user simply loses the seal on the cart header rather than seeing an incorrect one.

findings.contract_expects: OrderCustomerView.restaurant is OrderRestaurantRef which carries an optional `halal` field of type HalalBadge (required: [display_state]). HalalBadge is the product's single claim: when absent the client renders NO badge and reports a client error. The customer order view must be able to surface the restaurant's halal state.
findings.backend_emits: orderRestaurantRefDTO has exactly {id, name, logo_image_url}; there is no `halal` field on the struct at all, and OrderView carries no halal columns. loadOrderView SQL selects only restaurant_id and display_name from the restaurant join. The emitted restaurant ref can never carry a HalalBadge.
findings.evidence: openapi.yaml:8104-8118 (OrderRestaurantRef with halal: HalalBadge) & 8189-8211 vs services/hg/internal/orders/dto.go:201-205 (orderRestaurantRefDTO no halal) & map.go:89 & order_read.go:98,106 (SQL selects only r.display_name)

verdict.reasoning:
Verified against source. Contract: OrderRestaurantRef (openapi.yaml:8104-8118) declares `halal: $ref HalalBadge` as a property; HalalBadge (7189-7199) is required:[display_state] and per C-12 its absence makes the client render NO badge and report a client error. OrderCustomerView (8183-8211) requires `restaurant`, which resolves to OrderRestaurantRef. Go side confirms the omission on every cited line: orderRestaurantRefDTO (dto.go:201-205) is exactly {id json:"id", name json:"name", logo_image_url json:"logo_image_url"} with no halal field; orderViewToDTO (map.go:89) builds the ref as {ID, Name, LogoImageURL} only; loadOrderView SQL (order_read.go:96-114) selects only o.restaurant_id, r.display_name and NULL::text for the logo from the restaurant join, and OrderView has no halal columns/scan targets. So the emitted restaurant ref can never carry a HalalBadge — the claim's code reading is exact.

One correction to the claim's framing, which does NOT reduce severity: `halal` is OPTIONAL in OrderRestaurantRef (required:[id,name]), so a payload omitting it still VALIDATES against the contract despite additionalProperties:false. This is therefore not a hard schema-break/app-crash; the client won't fail JSON-schema validation. However, it is a genuine and permanent halal-field drift on a customer-facing surface: the customer order view will always surface no halal state, tripping the C-12 client-error path and violating non-negotiable invariant #8 ("a missing halal field renders no badge"). Halal is the product's single load-bearing claim, and the project rubric explicitly rates halal drifts critical. The drift is real and correctly rated critical on product/invariant grounds (not on app-crash grounds).

findings.contract_expects: OrderCustomerView.eta_at: type [string,'null'] format date-time — the customer-facing ETA the tracking UI renders.
findings.backend_emits: orderCustomerViewDTO has no eta_at JSON field; OrderView struct has no ETA field; SQL selects no eta column. The key is entirely absent from the wire body.
findings.evidence: openapi.yaml:8244-8246 (eta_at) vs services/hg/internal/orders/dto.go:178-199 (no eta_at) & order_read.go:17-49; consumer TrackingScreen.tsx:108 reads state.order.eta_at as estimatedAt — undefined, ETA never renders

verdict.reasoning:
Real drift, but the claimed "high" severity is overstated; corrected to low.

CONTRACT (confirmed): OrderCustomerView.eta_at exists at openapi.yaml:8244-8246, type [string,'null'], format date-time. CRITICAL CORRECTION to the claim: eta_at is NOT required. The schema's required[] is [id, code, state, restaurant, lines, money, placed_at] (openapi.yaml:8189). The generated client (packages/api-client/src/generated/openapi.d.ts:4269) types it as `eta_at?: string | null` — optional AND nullable. So the drift_type "missing_required_field" is mislabeled; it is a missing OPTIONAL field.

BACKEND (confirmed real): getOrder renders orderCustomerViewDTO via orderViewToDTO (map.go:85). Neither orderCustomerViewDTO (dto.go:178-199), the OrderView struct (order_read.go:17-49), nor the SQL SELECT (order_read.go:96-114) contains any eta_at/ETAAt field or column. The ETAAt field the evidence might be confused by (ordersread_dto.go:24) belongs to orderTrackingDTO — a DIFFERENT operation (getOrderTracking, /tracking endpoint), not getOrder. So for getOrder the eta_at key is genuinely absent from the wire body. The auditor's core code reading is correct.

CONSUMER / IMPACT (contradicts "high"): TrackingScreen.tsx:108 reads state.order.eta_at (typed string|null|undefined) and passes it to StatusTimeline's `estimatedAt?: string | null` prop. StatusTimeline guards with `{estimatedAt ? ...formatAbsoluteTime... : null}` (ui-native StatusTimeline.tsx:448; ui-web:329). Passing undefined to an optional prop is valid TypeScript and the component renders nothing rather than throwing. No app crash, no exception, no undefined-deref. It is not halal, money, or auth. The concrete effect is graceful degradation: the "Estimated <time>" line silently never appears in tracking.

Verdict: genuine backend↔contract drift (contract defines eta_at, a shipped consumer reads it, backend never emits it), so is_real=true. verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed real. The contract's 201 response for attachRestaurantDocument (openapi.yaml:2864-2874) wraps `data: KycDocument`. KycDocument (openapi.yaml:9185-9234) is `additionalProperties: false` with `required: [id, subject_type, doc_type, state, version, created_at]`, and names its date/issuer fields `valid_until`/`issuer`/`certificate_number`.

The backend handler (handler.go:287-292) returns `*DocumentRow` via `httpx.Respond`, which correctly wraps it in `{data: ...}` (respond.go:40-42), so the envelope matches — the drift is inside the data object. DocumentRow (store.go:69-78) serializes: id, subject_id, doc_type, state, stored_object_id, expires_on, issuer_name, created_at. AttachDocument (repo_reads.go:319-339) populates exactly those fields.

Field-by-field vs the schema:
- Missing REQUIRED `version` — schema requires integer; DocumentRow has no version field at all. A strict decoder rejects on missing required.
- Missing REQUIRED `subject_type` — not emitted.
- `expires_on` should be `valid_until` (wrong name) — extra prop under additionalProperties:false.
- `issuer_name` should be `issuer` (wrong name) — extra prop.
- `stored_object_id` — not in schema at all — extra prop.
- No `certificate_number`, `issued_on`, `rejection_reason_code`, `review_note`, `reviewed_at` (these are optional, so not fatal on their own).

This is not a misread: SQL/JSON tags and struct definition all confirm the emitted shape. With additionalProperties:false plus two missing required fields, a generated/strict client would fail to parse the 201, breaking the R-07 restaurant document-attach flow (which includes the HALAL_CERTIFICATE doc type). It is a genuine, consistent-with-the-list-endpoint drift.

Severity: high (not critical). It is client-breaking on a compliance-critical onboarding path, but it does not crash the server, corrupt money, or emit a wrong halal badge — the halal verification signal is not being falsified here, only the document metadata envelope is malformed. High is the correct rating.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED REAL (with a caveat on the drift_type label).

Contract (contracts/openapi.yaml, MenuItemVersion schema ~line 9435-9470): the schema is additionalProperties:false and defines both ingredients_text (type [string,'null']) and image_url (type [string,'null'], format uri) as properties. However required[] = [id, menu_item_id, version, review_status, created_at] — neither ingredients_text nor image_url is required, and both are nullable. So strictly, omitting them does NOT violate response schema validation; the claim's drift_type "missing_required_field" is imprecise. It is a missing-optional-field / semantic-completeness drift, not a required-field violation.

Backend truly emits neither field:
- DTO menuItemVersion (dto.go:477-492) has no ingredients_text and no image_url json tag at all.
- Both render paths omit them: renderMenuItemVersion (handler_menu.go:385-408) and the inline decide handler (handler_menu.go:359-374).
- The projection row struct menuItemVersionRow (store_menu.go:51-68) carries no IngredientsText or ImageObjectID field.
- The queue query ListMenuReviewQueue (store_menu.go:277-308) SELECTs description but never selects miv.ingredients_text or miv.image_object_id, and Scan never reads them.
- The store DOES persist ingredients_text and image_object_id on insert (store_menu.go:212-221), confirming the data exists in the table but is never read back onto the review queue.
- No image_url presigning exists anywhere in internal/admin (grep found ingredients/image only on the input path, handler_menu.go:142-175). image_url would additionally require presigning image_object_id, which is entirely absent.

The DTO comment at dto.go:474-476 is misleading: it only justifies omitting reviewed_by/updated_at and gives false assurance that every other named field is present.

Severity: high (not critical). The menu review queue is the human instrument by which claim-bearing menu fields — the ingredient words and the dish picture — are approved or rejected before going live. Dropping both from the wire means the admin reviews a halal-relevant item without seeing its ingredients text or image, defeating the purpose of the review gate and touching the platform's single load-bearing halal-verification claim. It is not critical because there is no crash, no money path, and no false halal badge emitted directly to end users; it degrades (not silently falsifies) the verification workflow. High is correct.

root_cause.why_it_passed:
No gate ever compares a byte emitted by the running Go server to contracts/openapi.yaml. The two gates check disjoint things and neither closes the loop.

Root `pnpm check` (package.json:18) = validate:contract + validate:fixtures + generate:check + generate:tokens:check + lint + typecheck. I read both TS scripts in tools/contract-tools/src/:
- validate-contract.ts lints the openapi.yaml document itself ($ref resolution, operationId casing, x-roles presence, the money/mass-assignment invariants, YAML-1.1 truthy traps). It parses the YAML and inspects it; it never issues an HTTP request.
- validate-fixtures.ts compiles the openapi.yaml as JSON-Schema-2020-12 (Ajv) and validates the 311 committed fixture JSON files under contracts/fixtures/ against the schema each fixture *names*. It validates static, hand/generator-built fixture files — not server output.
- generate:check regenerates the TS api-client and git-diffs it; generate:tokens:check does design tokens. typecheck/lint are static. So the entire root gate proves the contract is internally consistent and that fixtures + generated TS client match it. The Go server is never invoked by any of these.

Backend `make check` (Makefile:101) = fmt-check vet test; test = `go test -race ./...`. The Go tests that claim to be conformance tests (internal/admin/handler_orders_conformance_test.go, handler_menu_conformance_test.go, internal/rider/rider_shape_test.go, and the account/addresses/restaurant stage3/stage4 files) all assert against Go string literals hand-transcribed from the contract, not against openapi.yaml. Concretely:
- handler_menu_conformance_test.go:48-73 defines menuCategoryRequired/Optional, menuVersionRequired/Optional as []string, and the file header comment (lines 44-50) literally says the impl serves restaurant_id/created_at/updated_at which are 'NOT named by the MenuCategory schema' — then puts them in the `optional` allow-list anyway. The 'closed schema' check (assertMenuClosedObject) is only as correct as that hand-copied list.
- rider_shape_test.go:147 comments the enum vars are 'mirrored from contracts/openapi.yaml'; line 178 hard-codes the RiderMe key set as a literal.
- handler_orders_conformance_test.go:56-105 hard-codes adminViewRequired/adminViewOptional/orderMoneyRequired/etc. as []string.

So the 'conformance' assertion is: does the server match a human's transcription of the contract into Go slices? If the transcription is wrong, stale, or over-permissive (as the menu file admits), a non-conformant response passes. And the loop is never closed against the actual YAML.

Finally, the apps were built against the Prism mock on :4010, which serializes from the contract and therefore always emits contract-perfect shapes. The apps compiled against the generated TS client (whose types come from the contract), so at build time everything typechecked. The real Go server was substituted for the mock at runtime only, where no schema check runs — so drift surfaced only in the running product, not in any gate.
gaps: No test or CI step feeds a real Go server response body into an openapi.yaml-driven validator. The contract is never the oracle for server output; a hand-copied Go []string is.

The 'closed schema' Go tests re-implement additionalProperties:false / required against transcribed field lists, so any transcription error (e.g. menuCategoryOptional wrongly including restaurant_id/created_at/updated_at per the file's own comment) whitelists a real drift.
Enum membership is checked against hand-maintained Go maps (paymentStateEnum, menuReviewStatusEnum, enumOnboardingState, ...) that can silently fall behind the contract's 80 enums.

Coverage is incomplete and manual: only the handlers whose authors happened to write a *_conformance/*_shape test are checked at all. There is no enumeration that every 2xx response of every one of the 144 operations is validated. An operation with no shape test has zero conformance coverage.

The 311 fixtures (which DO cover every state) are validated against the contract but are never replayed against the server, and the server's live responses are never validated against the fixtures' schemas. The two truth sources never meet.

No generated Go response DTOs exist. go.mod has no getkin/kin-openapi and no oapi-codegen; the Go structs the handlers marshal are hand-written and free to diverge (field renamed 'occurred_at' vs contract 'at' is exactly the class of drift the tests were written after-the-fact to chase).
The mock on :4010 gave false confidence: apps validated shapes against a contract-perfect emitter, so integration against the mock could never reveal server drift.
root_cause.durable_fix:
Adopt option (a) as the primary durable mechanism, backed by (c) as the deeper 'unrepresentable' layer, with (b) folded in for free because the fixtures already carry the operationId+schema+status needed to drive it.

Assessment of the three options in the requested order:

(a) Response-conformance harness — RECOMMENDED, build first. Add a Go test package (e.g. services/hg/internal/conformance) that: loads contracts/openapi.yaml once via kin-openapi (openapi3.NewLoader ... LoadFromFile), builds an openapi3filter router (gorillamux router or routers/legacy), spins each domain's chi router in-process via httptest.NewServer (the tests already do this — buildRouter/buildAdminTestServer), and for every request it issues, runs openapi3filter.ValidateResponse against the matched operation's declared 2xx schema. Because the schemas use additionalProperties:false and required[...], kin-openapi rejects extra fields, missing required fields, wrong types, and open-enum values automatically — no hand-copied []string. This replaces the entire hand-transcribed apparatus in handler_orders_conformance_test.go / handler_menu_conformance_test.go / rider_shape_test.go with one contract-driven validator. Feasible: the doc is clean 3.1 with operationId + application/json response schemas on every op (verified on getOrderAdmin at openapi.yaml:5218-5229), $ref-internal-only (validate-contract.ts already proves refs resolve), and additionalProperties:false present. Cost: add getkin/kin-openapi to go.mod (single dep) + a helper that wraps `do()`/`doJSON()` to validate on the way out. This is the mechanism that makes a non-conformant Go response FAIL the gate.

(b) Fixture replay against the real server — RECOMMENDED as a complementary corpus, low extra cost. The 311 fixtures already declare {operations[], schema, status, payload}. Two ways to use them: (i) as an ADDITIONAL response-schema source in the same harness — after a live call, validate the live body against BOTH the operation's contract schema AND (when a fixture for that operation/state exists) round-trip the fixture's own schema to confirm agreement; (ii) drive request scenarios: for state-machine seeds, seed the DB to the fixture's state, hit the operation, and assert the live response validates against the same component schema the fixture names. Replaying the fixtures as *expected bodies* byte-for-byte is brittle (ids/timestamps differ — the fixture menu_version_approved.json even has an APPROVED version carrying rejection_reason_code, which the conformance test forbids), so replay should assert schema-conformance + invariants, not equality. Net: (b) mainly buys state coverage; the validation engine is still (a).

(c) Generate Go response DTOs FROM the contract — RECOMMENDED as the eventual floor, larger change. oapi-codegen can emit Go types for all component schemas from openapi.yaml (mirror of what the TS api-client already does). If every handler's response value is one of these generated types, a renamed/extra/missing field is a compile error, and drift becomes unrepresentable rather than test-detectable. This is the strongest fix but requires refactoring existing hand-written DTOs to the generated ones (and the generated additionalProperties:false structs must be marshaled with a disallow-unknown discipline). Do it after (a) is catching drift, because (a) is cheap, immediate, and needs no handler rewrite; (c) is the durable end-state that removes the whole class.

Bottom line: (a) now (fail the gate on any non-conformant 2xx body, contract-driven), (b) layered on to get all-states coverage from the existing 311 fixtures, (c) as the follow-up that turns drift into a compile error.

root_cause.unrepresentable_option:
Feasible and worth doing as the end-state, but it is a larger change than the harness.

Mechanism: run oapi-codegen against contracts/openapi.yaml to emit Go structs for all component schemas (the mirror of packages/api-client, which already proves the contract generates clean typed clients). Handlers then construct and marshal ONLY those generated types for their 2xx responses. A renamed field ('occurred_at' vs the contract's 'at'), an extra field, or a missing required field becomes a Go compile error, so drift is unrepresentable rather than test-caught. Add a git-diff gate on the generated Go package (exactly like generate:check does for the TS client at package.json:10) so the generated code cannot be hand-edited or fall stale.

Feasibility evidence: the doc is OpenAPI 3.1 with internal-only $refs (validate-contract.ts confirms all refs resolve), every operation has an operationId, response schemas are named components with additionalProperties:false (verified on getOrderAdmin at openapi.yaml:5218-5229), and the same document already round-trips through JSON-Schema tooling (Ajv in validate-fixtures.ts) and through the TS generator. So codegen input is sound. Caveats: (1) oapi-codegen's 3.1 support has historically trailed 3.0 for some keyword edge cases (nullable via type arrays, some allOf compositions like OrderAdminView = OrderCustomerView + admin extension) — those specific schemas need a generation smoke-test. (2) Go structs do not enforce additionalProperties:false on the *marshal* side by themselves; you must marshal via the generated types and avoid map[string]any escape hatches for it to be a true compile-time guarantee. (3) It requires refactoring every handler that currently returns a hand-written DTO. Recommendation: ship the kin-openapi response-validation harness first (catches drift immediately, no handler rewrite), then adopt generated response DTOs to convert the residual runtime check into a compile-time impossibility.

report.executive_summary:
The HalalGoes Go backend has drifted from contracts/openapi.yaml across ~79 confirmed findings (7 critical, 21 high, 25 medium, 26 low). Nothing in CI ever compares a byte the running server emits against the contract — both gates check disjoint, contract-internal things — so drift surfaced only in the running product. Lead with the three tiers that matter:

HALAL (the product's single claim): Three surfaces guaranteed to render NO halal seal by construction. GET /v1/cart emits "restaurant": null unconditionally (cartToDTO never assigns Restaurant; the store never even fetches halal data), so the cart — a halal re-assertion surface before checkout — never shows the seal (critical). GET /v1/restaurant/profile emits a flat halal_status string instead of the required `halal` HalalBadge object, so the restaurant profile cannot express display_state (critical). GET /v1/orders/{orderId} (customer view) omits OrderRestaurantRef.halal entirely, tripping the C-12 client-error path (critical). addCartLine inherits the same null-restaurant defect (high). None produce a FALSE badge — the client fails safe to no-badge (invariant #8 holds) — but the required halal presentation is absent platform-wide on these surfaces.

MONEY + APP-CRASH: The restaurant-web order screens are the worst blast radius. The backend serves its own OrderDetailView / OrderSummaryView (flat total_cents/subtotal_cents/currency, no nested `money`, no `customer`, no `lines`) where the contract requires the nested OrderRestaurantView. restaurant-web reads order.money.subtotal_cents / commission_cents / restaurant_net_cents and order.customer.display_name — all undefined at runtime — so the Order Detail and Order Queue screens throw TypeError and crash. This is BOTH a money-display path (the restaurant cannot see what it will be paid: commission_cents / restaurant_net_cents are never even queried) AND an app crash. Every state-transition endpoint (acceptOrder, rejectOrder, markOrderReady, delayOrder) returns the same wrong-shaped struct, so the crash recurs after every successful action. rejectOrder and delayOrder additionally 422 on input (wrong field names: `reason` vs `reason_code`, `delay_minutes` vs `added_minutes`) under DisallowUnknownFields, so reject and delay are broken end-to-end before the response even matters.

ROOT CAUSE: No response-conformance oracle exists. Go "conformance" tests assert against hand-transcribed []string field lists (one file's own comment admits it whitelists non-contract fields), enum checks use hand-maintained Go maps, coverage is only whatever handler authors happened to test, and the apps were built against the Prism mock on :4010 which always emits contract-perfect shapes — so drift was structurally invisible until the real server ran. The durable fix (do it first) is a kin-openapi response-validation harness that runs every handler's live 2xx body through openapi3filter.ValidateResponse against openapi.yaml, making additionalProperties:false / required[] / enums the automatic oracle.

systemic_patterns: Backend serves its own hand-written view struct instead of the contract schema — the single largest pattern. OrderDetailView / OrderSummaryView (flat money, no customer, no lines) is returned where every restaurant-order operation contractually requires the nested OrderRestaurantView. Fixing the one shared struct-to-DTO mapping (nest money as RestaurantOrderMoney, add customer OrderCustomerRef, populate lines as OrderLine, add delivery_area/is_late/promised_ready_at) fixes getRestaurantOrder, listRestaurantOrders, acceptOrder, rejectOrder, markOrderReady, and delayOrder at once.

Halal claim dropped by omission — cartToDTO never assigns Restaurant, orderRestaurantRefDTO has no halal field, and RestaurantProfile emits a flat halal_status string instead of the `halal` HalalBadge object. The store SQL never even fetches halal certification data for cart/order joins. One fix pattern: every restaurant reference on the wire (cart, order, profile) must carry a populated HalalBadge, which requires widening the store queries to join halal_certificate + halal_issuing_body (the catalog domain already does this via toHalalBadge — reuse it).

Input DTOs use the wrong JSON field name AND decode strictly — reason vs reason_code (rejectOrder), delay_minutes/reason vs added_minutes/reason_code (delayOrder), promised_ready_minutes vs prep_eta_minutes + missing accepted_note (acceptOrder), is_available bool vs availability_state enum (setMenuItemAvailability), plus omitted optional fields (allergens_declared, image_object_id, prep_minutes on create/updateMenuItem, unavailable_menu_item_ids on reject). Because handlers call decodeStrict/DisallowUnknownFields, any contract-correct client is rejected with 422. One fix pattern: align every request DTO's json tags to the contract input schema and add the missing optional fields.

Nested object flattened to top-level fields — RestaurantProfile.address (PublicAddress) emitted as flat line1/city/province/..., RestaurantHours.intervals emitted as `hours`, RestaurantOrderMoney flattened to top-level total_cents/subtotal_cents. Same wrong-nesting shape across profile, hours, and orders; a contract-driven DTO mapper eliminates the class.

additionalProperties:false violations from extra fields the struct carries — halal_status/created_at/updated_at on RestaurantProfile, item_count/state_since/reject_reason on order views, status on the onboarding submit response. Strict validators reject these even when required fields are present. Generating response DTOs from the contract (oapi-codegen) makes both the extra-field and missing-field classes unrepresentable.

Missing/hardcoded-constant values on populated data — cuisines always []string{} (restaurant_cuisine used only for filtering, never projected), logo_image_url hardcoded NULL::text, CartLine.image_url never selected, current_price_cents/PRICE_CHANGED never computed. The data exists in the DB but the SELECT list never projects it; one pattern is widening the card/cart SELECT column set and populating the mapper.

No response-conformance oracle in either gate — the meta-pattern behind all of the above. Go tests assert against hand-transcribed []string field lists and hand-maintained enum maps; apps were built against the contract-perfect Prism mock. Every drift shape above is exactly what a kin-openapi ValidateResponse harness would have caught automatically via additionalProperties:false + required[] + enum membership.

prioritized_fix_plan.work: Build the durable response-conformance harness FIRST (root-cause fix). Add getkin/kin-openapi to services/hg/go.mod.
